title: Scheduled Launch Capacity Safeguard & Post-Event Incident Template
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary
-------
This playbook defines the SRE runbook and post-event incident template for scheduled, high-impact launches (marketing campaigns, partner integrations, large customer migrations). It covers pre-launch SLO/error-budget gating, capacity booking and reservations, operational tooling to validate run readiness, live-day safeguards and escalation paths, and a structured post-event incident review that combines reliability and business impact analysis. Use this when a launch is expected to increase QPS, unique session length, or bursty embedding/chat workloads > 5x baseline for more than 30 minutes.

Goals
-----
- Protect tiered SLOs while maximizing launch throughput and customer experience.
- Provide a repeatable pre-launch checklist that ties capacity pledges to error budget impact.
- Define live-day operational controls and automated throttles to prevent prolonged SLO burn.
- Standardize post-event incident reviews to capture capacity-forensics, model-quality regressions, and customer impact.

Scope and applicability
----------------------
- Applies to any coordinated external launch that will materially change request profile for hosted/Dedicated/private tenants.
- Not intended for routine deployments (< 10% traffic change) or internal A/B experiments below canary threshold.
- Cross-functional stakeholders: Product launch owner, Platform PM, SRE oncall, Model owner, Customer Success.

Pre-launch: decision criteria and gating
--------------------------------------
1) Risk assessment (owner: Product launch owner)
   - Expected peak multiplier (QPS): <value> (example: 6x baseline)
   - Session length shift: median token count change (e.g., +40%)
   - % traffic to new model variant / unvalidated prompt sets
   - Business-critical SLAs during launch window (e.g., 99.9% p50 latency; 99.5% p99)

2) Error-budget gating (owner: SRE lead)
   - For the service(s) affected, compute projected error budget burn over launch window using historical traffic and synthetic canaries.
   - Gating rule: proceed only if projected burn keeps the monthly error-budget consumption <= 60% unless an approved risk waiver is recorded.

3) Capacity reservation and verification (owner: Capacity/Infra)
   - Reserve headroom: min(reserved_gpu_tokens, projected_peak_tokens * 1.25).
   - Reserve a warm-pool of model hot-pools: N warm instances per region (recommended: baseline_hotpool * 0.5 rounded up).
   - Test plan: run synthetic workload with 1.0x, 2.5x, and expected_peak multiplier for at least 15m each and capture latency, KV cache hit rates, GPU memory pressure.

Example capacity reservation request (JSON)
| payload |
{
  "tenant": "marketing-campaign-aug25",
  "start": "2025-08-25T10:00:00Z",
  "end": "2025-08-25T14:00:00Z",
  "peak_qps_estimate": "12000",
  "model_profile": "gpt-4x-infer-8k-quant",
  "hot_pool_instances": "12",
  "reserve_reason": "Public launch - campaign"
}

Operational tooling readiness checklist (owner: Platform/Tooling)
- Canary pipelines validated and toggles wired to traffic router (feature flags and routing policies).
- Telemetry retention for launch window: increase sampling to 100% for p95/p99 latency, error types, and tokenized model outputs for 24h post-launch.
- Synthetic canary jobs scheduled and healthy: canary-id, last-success timestamp.
- Automated throttle guard configured: error_budget_controller and traffic_shepherding policy attached to tenant.
- Model shadowing enabled where feasible: mirror 10–20% of traffic to new variant for quality checks without user-facing exposure.

Live-day runbook (owner: SRE oncall / Launch coordinator)
1) T-minus 60m: final readiness check
   - Confirm capacity reservations are active and warm pools at target.
   - Confirm datadog/telemetry dashboards show expected synthetic baseline.
2) T-minus 15m: enable expanded sampling and reduced aggregation windows (1m).
3) Launch start: staged ramp strategy (owner: Traffic Ops)
   - Stage 0 (0–5m): 5% traffic to new route. Verify latency p50/p95 and error-rate.
   - Stage 1 (5–20m): escalate to 25% if no SLO regression and error budget controller reports < 10% incremental burn.
   - Stage 2 (20–60m): escalate to 60–80% depending on business target.
   - Full ramp after 60m if all indicators green.
4) Real-time decision thresholds (automated & manual)
   - Auto-abort if p99 latency > baseline_p99 * 3 OR 5xx rate > baseline_5xx * 4 sustained for 3m.
   - Soft throttle if projected error budget burn rate exceeds 15% of remaining monthly budget within a 30m window.
   - Manual rollback if model-quality alerts detect >3% semantic regression on held prompt set or if customer-impacting errors observed for >10m.
5) Runbook escalation matrix
   - Pager: SRE oncall -> Platform lead -> Model owner -> Product launch owner.
   - Slack channel: #launches-live (pinned runbook link and incident playbook).

Telemetry and alerting specifics (owner: Observability)
- Required metrics (per-route and per-model): qps, p50/p95/p99 latency, 5xx rate, token consumption, KV cache hit ratio, GPU memory pressure, scheduling latency.
- Alert types and thresholds:
| Metric | Alert | Priority | Action |
| p99 latency | p99 > baseline*2 for 5m | P1 | Auto-throttle + page SRE |
| 5xx rate | 5xx rate > baseline*3 for 3m | P1 | Auto-abort route + page SRE |
| error-budget-burn-rate | projected > 25% remaining in 1h | P2 | Throttle recommendations to traffic ops |
| model-quality-regression | semantic-score drop > 2% vs baseline set | P1 | Mirror traffic to fallback, page model owner |

Automated tooling snippets
- Example CLI to create a temporary traffic gate:
  redwood traffic create-gate --tenant marketing-campaign-aug25 --rule "percent=0.05,condition=metrics.p99<2000" --expires "2025-08-25T11:00:00Z"

- Example alert rule (YAML):
alert: Launch_P99_Throttling
expr: rate_latency_p99{route="marketing-campaign"}[5m] > baseline_p99 * 2
for: 5m
labels:
  severity: critical
annotations:
  runbook: "/confluence/eng-sre/reliability-initiatives/scheduled-launch-capacity-safeguard-and-postmortem-template-2025"

Live forensic capture guidance
- When an alert fires during a launch, immediately enable launch-mode traces for the affected route for at least 30m.
- Capture the following artifacts into the incident evidence bucket:
  - telemetry snapshot (1m resolution) for 30m before and after alert
  - sampled request/response payloads (redacted) for model-quality triage
  - GPU host metrics timeseries and scheduler logs
  - traffic router decisions (which nodes served which tokens)

Post-event incident review: template and required deliverables (owner: SRE/Incident Lead)
1) Executive summary (required)
   - One-paragraph summary: what happened, impact to customers, duration, and resolution.
2) Timeline of key events (required)
   - Structured timeline with timestamps, actor (automation or human), and decision.
3) Data and metrics appendix (required)
   - Include time-series charts and a table of key KPIs: baseline vs observed (QPS, p50/p95/p99, error-rate, token consumption, error budget consumed during window).
   - Example KPI table:
| KPI | Baseline | Peak during launch | % delta |
| QPS | 2,000 | 12,000 | 500% |
| p99 latency | 800ms | 2,400ms | 200% |
| monthly error budget used | 15% | +18% during window | n/a |
4) Root cause hypothesis and validation steps (required)
   - Enumerate hypotheses and evidence supporting or refuting each.
5) Operational actions taken (required)
   - Describe throttles, rollbacks, and config changes performed, with timestamps.
6) Business impact and follow-up (required)
   - Customer tickets created, credits issued, and cost delta for extra capacity.
7) Postmortem remediation plan (required)
   - Owners, priority, expected completion dates, and verification criteria.
   - Example remediation items: optimize KV cache warm-up to reduce cold-start p99 by 30% (owner: runtime team, due: 2025-09-30).
8) Lessons learned for future launches (required)
   - Concrete changes to the pre-launch checklist or tooling.

SLO & capacity change recommendations after a launch
- If launch burned >60% of monthly error budget, schedule a retrospective to reassess monthly SLOs and tenant admission policies.
- Consider temporary SLO relaxations with explicit customer communication only when: business critical and after approval by product + SRE director.
- Update capacity projection model inputs with real observed peak multiplier, session length shift, and quantized-model memory usage.

Ownership matrix (table)
| Role | Responsible | Contact / Pager |
| Product launch owner | Defines business targets and tolerances | product+launch@redwood.ai |
| SRE lead | Error-budget gating, runbook authority | sre-lead@redwood.ai |
| Capacity/Infra | Reservations and hot-pool ops | infra-capacity@redwood.ai |
| Observability | Dashboards, alerts, forensic snapshots | observability@redwood.ai |
| Model owner | Quality regression triage and rollback | model-owner@redwood.ai |

Approval and waiver process
- If pre-launch error-budget gating fails, a waiver may be requested with: justification, compensating controls, and explicit rollback criteria. Approval required from SRE director and Product VP. Record waiver in the launch ticket and link to this playbook.

Runbook maintenance and periodic exercises
- Runbook owner: SRE lead (review cadence: quarterly).
- Mandatory tabletop exercise: run a simulated launch twice per year with synthetic traffic and at least one cross-functional incident drill reproducing an auto-abort scenario.

Appendix: sample postmortem checklist (quick reference)
1) Link incident page and capture evidence artifacts.
2) Produce executive summary and timeline within 48 hours.
3) Complete remediation plan with owners within 7 days.
4) Publish postmortem and schedule follow-up verification within 30 days.
